system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
Seller labels do not constrain the review; all items below remain buyer-side issues.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General warranty cap at **20% / $4.8m**. | Higher cap, ideally 50–100% for business warranties, with separate uncapped/carve-out categories. | **Reject 20% as the sole cap** — it is inadequate against the identified revenue, debt, IP and privacy exposures. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | $25,000 de minimis; $250,000 deductible basket. | Lower de minimis and basket; aggregation of related claims; no thresholds for fundamental, tax, IP, indemnity or fraud claims. | **Narrow materially** — the proposed thresholds could exclude real losses, especially repeat or related issues. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | Notice within 18 months; Seller seeks to apply limitations to all claims unless expressly excluded. | At least 24 months for general warranties; longer, tailored periods for tax, IP, data/privacy, employment and regulatory matters. | **Reject universal 18-month application** — several disclosed risks may emerge only after Completion. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limit. | Fundamental/title claims uncapped (or capped at purchase price), no basket/de minimis, and a substantially longer survival period. | **Reject** — ownership and capacity risks should not share an ordinary business-warranty regime. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all claims “of any nature”; no express fraud carve-out. | Express preservation of rights for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and deliberate/reckless misconduct; no cap, time limit or exclusive-remedy restriction. | **Insert an unequivocal fraud carve-out** — the present drafting could improperly seek to limit remedies for dishonesty. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the entire data room, accounts, registers and public records. | Specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties; indexed documents alone should not qualify warranties unless their relevance and nature are clearly disclosed. | **Delete or severely limit general disclosure** — data-room dumping shifts Seller warranty risk to Buyer without meaningful disclosure. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer/advisers or discoverable in data room/public records. | Restrict to Buyer’s actual knowledge of specified deal-team individuals, with no constructive-knowledge or adviser-imputation standard. | **Delete “discoverable” and adviser knowledge wording** — it converts diligence access into a warranty exclusion. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; regards consent as addressed on delivery of written consent. Disclosure confirms no final consent or evidence conditions are satisfied. | Bluefen consent and all conditions precedent to its effectiveness as a Completion condition; termination/right to defer or a specific indemnity and holdback if not obtained. | **Make this a hard CP** — Bluefen represents about $3.6m / 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approx. $3.2m debt/security to be released after Completion. Disclosure confirms it remains outstanding and undischargeed. | Repayment and unconditional discharge/release of all security at or before Completion, evidenced in the funds flow; no Buyer liability. | **Require simultaneous Completion discharge** — a post-Completion release conflicts with debt-free/cash-free delivery. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | $420,000 Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; Seller treats them as its matter. Payroll tax, super and on-costs unstated. | Seller-funded payment or a purchase-price reduction/escrow covering bonuses and all employment on-costs; clear allocation and discharge evidence. | **Put the full amount and on-costs in funds flow or adjust price** — otherwise Buyer inherits a Completion-triggered liability. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Specific indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; $180,000 remains open and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is provided. | Broad, uncapped specific indemnity for ownership/use of all SOW3 materials and related claims, plus payment/assignment evidence or escrow/retention. | **Expand and secure the indemnity** — non-payment may prevent transfer of key IP. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Treated as preliminary/not expected material; no confirmed access, scope or notification conclusion. | Full investigation, preservation/remediation, regulatory and affected-person notification compliance, tailored warranties and uncapped/specific indemnity or escrow. | **Do not accept the “preliminary” characterisation** — potential privacy/regulatory exposure cannot be assessed yet. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling $330,000 said to be ordinary-course costs. Disclosure does not establish avoidability, term, accrual or ordinary-course status. | Full contracts and timing; confirmation of authority, ordinary-course status, termination rights and treatment as debt/working-capital or leakage where appropriate. | **Require evidence and an economic adjustment if needed** — “ordinary course” does not answer whether Buyer is locked into unbudgeted commitments. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Seller seeks all limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to apply to every claim; tax and IP are said settled under general regime. | Separate regimes for fundamental/title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, debt/leakage, privacy and fraud, each with appropriate caps and survival. | **Insist on express category carve-outs** — a general regime must not dilute higher-risk or known exposures. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller holds 100%; disclosure says Buyer must conduct its own verification. | Title warranty, no encumbrances/security interests/options, valid transfer deliverables, register update and PPSR/company-search confirmation at Completion. | **Do not rely only on DD-012** — the register is evidence, not a substitute for contractual title protection and completion deliverables. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP positions are settled under the general regime. | Standalone tax covenant/indemnity with tax-specific survival and no ordinary caps; robust IP warranties, ownership chain evidence and appropriate indemnity. | **Reject “general regime” treatment** — tax and IP are specialist, potentially long-tail risks requiring bespoke allocation. |
=== END ADVICE ===
